title: HMW DNA extraction from diverse plants species for PacBio and Nanopore sequencing
author: Alessia Russo
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5t7g6rn

steps.title: Grind leaf tissue in LN2
steps.instruction: Flash‑freeze ~100‑110 mg leaf tissue in liquid nitrogen, grind in a pre‑chilled mortar and pestle until the powder is as fine as wheat flour, adding liquid nitrogen continuously to keep the material frozen; store the powder at –80 °C until use.

steps.title: Warm SDS Lysis Buffer
steps.instruction: Aliquot 600 µl SDS Lysis Buffer into a 2 ml tube per sample, incubate at 65 °C for at least 30 min (mix gently every 10 min) and keep the buffer warm until the tissue powder is added; perform all steps under a fume hood because the protocol uses BME, phenol and chloroform.

steps.title: Add tissue powder and vortex
steps.instruction: Add ~50‑100 mg tissue powder (1‑2 spoons SP SCIENCEWARE 0.10 ml) to the warm Lysis Buffer, vortex immediately for 3‑5 seconds to homogenize (avoid >100 mg to prevent reduced A260/230 purity).

steps.title: Incubate lysate at 55°C
steps.instruction: Incubate the lysate for 20 min at 55 °C with gentle agitation (≤400 rpm in a thermomixer or water bath); after 10 min invert the tube gently 10 times.

steps.title: Add RNase A and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 4 µl of 100 mg/ml RNase A, invert the tube gently 10 times, then incubate 10 min at 55 °C with gentle agitation.

steps.title: Add potassium acetate and mix
steps.instruction: Add 200 µl of 5 M potassium acetate (KAc); mix by pipetting up and down 5 times with a P1000 cut tip and invert the tube 5 times to obtain a homogeneous solution that precipitates proteins and polysaccharides.

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Work under a fume hood. Either (a) add 800 µl phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (pH 8) or (b) add 400 µl phenol (pH 8), invert, then add 400 µl chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24:1).

steps.title: Incubate on rotator
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture for 10 min on a rotator at 20 rpm.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 10 min at 10 000 g at room temperature; transfer the upper aqueous phase (usually 700‑800 µl) to a new 2 ml tube using a P1000 cut tip, pipetting slowly to avoid shearing DNA and avoiding any interphase or lower organic layer.

steps.title: Chloroform‑isoamyl alcohol wash
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24:1) to the transferred aqueous phase, incubate at room temperature for 10 min with gentle agitation (20 rpm), then centrifuge 10 min at 10 000 g (RT). Transfer the resulting supernatant to a fresh 2 ml tube, avoiding interphase, and record the final volume.

steps.title: Prepare and add bead solution
steps.instruction: Vortex the magnetic bead solution for 30 seconds to fully resuspend beads, then add 1 volume of bead solution to the sample (1:1 v/v).

steps.title: Incubate beads on rotator
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube on a rotator at 10 rpm for 20‑30 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Magnetic separation and discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Spin down for 1 second, place the tube on a magnetic rack, wait until beads collect at the tube wall and the solution becomes clear (a few minutes), then carefully remove and discard the supernatant without disturbing the bead pellet.

steps.title: First 70% ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml of 70 % ethanol to the bead pellet, invert the tube gently 20 times to resuspend (aggregates are acceptable).

steps.title: Magnetic separation after ethanol
steps.instruction: Spin down for 1 second, place the tube on the magnetic rack until the solution clears, then remove the ethanol supernatant without disturbing the beads.

steps.title: Repeat ethanol washes (2‑4 total)
steps.instruction: Repeat the ethanol‑wash steps (add 1 ml 70 % ethanol, invert 20×, magnetic separation, remove supernatant) two to three additional times; a total of 2‑4 washes is typical, with 2 usually sufficient.

steps.title: Remove residual ethanol with P10
steps.instruction: Spin down for 1 second and use a P10 pipette to remove any remaining ethanol from the bead pellet.

steps.title: Elute DNA with EB or Tris
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl of Elution Buffer (EB) or Tris‑HCl 10 mM pH 8.5, then resuspend the beads completely by gentle swirling or flicking the tube.

steps.title: Incubate eluate at 37°C
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 37 °C for 15 minutes and flick the tube once more to aid elution.

steps.title: Final magnetic separation and collect DNA
steps.instruction: Spin down for 1 second, place the tube on a magnetic rack until beads bind (may take longer for high‑concentration DNA); optionally leave overnight at RT or add extra EB, mixing by flicking, then remove the clear eluate containing DNA.

steps.title: Transfer DNA and relax overnight
steps.instruction: Transfer the eluted DNA to a new tube using a cut tip or wide‑bore tip (DNA is viscous); leave the tube at room temperature overnight to allow the high‑molecular‑weight DNA to relax and homogenize.

steps.title: Measure purity and concentration
steps.instruction: Measure absorbance at 230, 260 and 280 nm with a spectrophotometer (e.g., NanoDrop 2000); acceptable ratios are A260/280 = 1.8‑2.0 and A260/230 = 2.0‑2.2. Determine dsDNA concentration with a fluorometric assay (e.g., Qubit 3.0 BR assay); the NanoDrop/Qubit concentration ratio should be < 2.

steps.title: Assess DNA integrity
steps.instruction: Evaluate DNA integrity on a TapeStation and assess fragment length distribution using a PhermoPulse system or pulsed‑field gel electrophoresis (PFGE).

steps.title: Optional additional bead purification
steps.instruction: If needed, pool elutions from multiple tubes, incubate fresh bead solution (pre‑incubated >30 min at RT and vortexed 20 seconds) with the pooled DNA, then repeat steps 12‑21 (bead binding, ethanol washes, elution) to improve A260/280 and A260/230 ratios.
